issue.body:
### 🐛 Describe the bug

The following is AI analysis edited for clarity:

> On ROCm, `torch.compile` produces wrong values for `torch.as_strided(x, size, stride, 0)`
when `x` is a graph input that is a view with a non-zero `storage_offset()`.

> Since #184232, Inductor translates explicit storage-relative `as_strided` offsets onto
the graph input's runtime data pointer. That is, `storage_offset - x.storage_offset()`.

> For example, for a view at offset 6 that is `as_strided` back to offset 0, the generated Triton kernel
loads at `in_ptr0 + (-6 + x0)`. So the generated Triton kernel loads in at negative offsets from the pointer it
was handed. On CUDA this is ordinary pointer arithmetic and the result is correct. On
ROCm the elements at negative offsets read back as 0, so the pointer is now in the wrong position.

> This is pre-existing on `main`. #192227 only adds a test that exercises it on GPU (the
test added in #184232 runs on CPU), which is how it surfaced.

### Minimum Reproducing Example

The following is an AI generated minimum reproducing example

```python
import torch

def fn(x):
    return torch.as_strided(x, (12,), (1,), 0) + 1.0

base = torch.arange(12, dtype=torch.float32, device="cuda")
x = base[6:9]  # storage_offset() == 6

print(fn(x))                 # [1., 2., ..., 12.]
print(torch.compile(fn)(x))  # ROCm: [1., 1., 1., 1., 1., 1., 7., ..., 12.]
```

> Equivalent test: `PYTORCH_TEST_WITH_ROCM=1 python test/inductor/test_torchinductor.py GPUTests.test_as_strided_past_input_extent_cuda`

### Observed in CI (linux-jammy-rocm-py3.10-mi350, gfx950)

```
AssertionError: Tensor-likes are not close!
Mismatched elements: 5 / 12 (41.7%)
Greatest absolute difference: 5.0 at index (5,) (up to 1e-05 allowed)
```

> Indices 0-5 (the six loads at offsets -6..-1 from the input pointer) all come back as
0 + 1.0; index 0 happens to match because its expected value is also 1.0. Indices 6-11
(non-negative offsets) are correct.

- https://github.com/pytorch/pytorch/actions/runs/33675357509/job/100405054717
- https://github.com/pytorch/pytorch/actions/runs/33675357509/job/100405054641
- https://github.com/pytorch/pytorch/actions/runs/33675357509/job/100405054556

I don't have access to any AMD hardware, so we don't have a smoking gun on the cause, however my agent suggested this may be a good place to start.

> The Triton AMD backend enables buffer ops by default (`knobs.amd.use_buffer_ops`,
env `AMDGCN_USE_BUFFER_OPS`, default `True` at the CI pin c01b6774b) and specializes
tensor args whose storage is <= 2GB with `tt.pointer_range=32`. AMD buffer loads take an
unsigned 32-bit offset and return 0 for out-of-range offsets, which matches a negative
offset relative to the kernel's base pointer reading back 0. Running the repro with
`AMDGCN_USE_BUFFER_OPS=0` should confirm or rule this out.

issue.title: [ROCm][Inductor] `as_strided` on a graph-input view reads back zeros when the rebased offset is negative

issue.body:
## Issue

Fixes https://github.com/pytorch/pytorch/issues/192226

## Summary

AI Analysis:
> A view with a non-zero `storage_offset` passed as a mutated pointer argument to a raw `triton.jit` kernel was silently miscompiled. Functionalization clones such an argument with `clone_preserve_strides()`, which reads `storage_offset + span` elements out of the tensor's storage; that is fine in eager, but Inductor materializes an intermediate view as a buffer sized to the view alone, so the leading `storage_offset` elements lie outside any allocation, and the `as_strided` lowering reinterpreted past the buffer with no extent check. Any element the kernel chose not to write therefore came back holding freed memory. This PR stops the clone from requesting storage the tensor does not own — a plain `clone()` for a dense tensor, which reproduces its strides at offset 0 and is all a kernel needs since it only sees a data pointer plus strides, or a clone through the base when the view has gaps, via a new opt-in `base=` keyword on `clone_preserve_strides` — and makes the `as_strided` lowering raise instead of silently reinterpreting past a realized buffer, so any other producer of this pattern fails loudly rather than corrupting data. See #192219 for the full mechanism and the generated code. Suggested review order is `torch/_prims_common` (the opt-in `base=`), then `triton_kernel_wrap` (which clone is chosen, and why the base has to be threaded through the HOP), then `lowering.py` (the backstop), then `post_grad.py`, then the tests; the commit message records the two alternatives I tried and rejected.

My Analysis:
When using torch compile, an intermediate tensor buffer of a view is materialized. The indexing into that view though is based on the original tensor, which can be larger due to offset and striding. This results in out of bounds reads on view's allocated buffer. This PR fixes the issue by both making it so that the global indexing doesn't happen on the view's buffer, but also adds more defensive code by having guards on the bounds of the view which result in raised exceptions instead of silently failing (which IMO is the worst possible buggy behavior).

## Checklist

AI Analysis:
> - [x] Passes lint (`spin fixlint`)
> - [x] Added/updated tests
> - [ ] Updated documentation (if applicable)
> - [ ] Included benchmark results (for PRs impacting perf)

> Not a perf change in intent, but it reduces copying: for the repro in the issue the clones move 8192 elements total instead of 20480, since each clone now spans only the view rather than the view plus everything ahead of it in the storage.

My analysis:
We actually get a minor performance boost now that we only clone the appropriate storage size for the view's buffer.

Ran the linting and tests. I don't think this requires documentation changes beyond the comments that were already left.

## BC-breaking?

AI Analysis:
> No. `clone_preserve_strides()` gains a keyword-only `base=` argument that defaults to the existing behaviour, so every current caller is unchanged. The new extent check in the `as_strided` lowering can turn a previously silent miscompile into a `NotImplementedError`; graph inputs are exempt, because their real storage may legitimately extend past the layout and Inductor already rebases the offset onto the incoming pointer.

My analysis:
The only difference is in the case when previously we would have silently been in undefined behavior due to garbage memory reads, where we now simply just raise and exception instead.

issue.body:
# [ROCm][Inductor] Skip AMD buffer ops when as_strided rebases to a negative offset

Fixes https://github.com/pytorch/pytorch/issues/195823

### Summary

HIP Triton buffer ops cannot execute the negative load index produced when Inductor rebases `as_strided` onto a graph-input view. Disable `pointer_range_32` for those kernels and unskip the ROCm GPU test.

### Problem

After #184232, a storage-relative `as_strided` offset is rewritten onto the graph input's runtime `data_ptr()`. For a view at `storage_offset=6` that is as_strided back to offset 0, the kernel loads at `in_ptr0 + (-6 + i)`.

On CUDA that is ordinary 64-bit pointer arithmetic. On HIP, Triton AMD buffer ops (`tt.pointer_range=32`, default on) take an unsigned 32-bit offset from the kernel pointer and return 0 for out-of-range values. Indices before the view pointer therefore read back as 0: compiled `[1., 1., 1., 1., 1., 1., 7., …, 12.]` vs eager `[1., 2., …, 12.]`.

#192227 added `test_as_strided_past_input_extent`, which is `@skipIfRocm` on `main`. This is that skip, not a new lowering bug.

### Change

Extend the existing HIP carve-out that already turns off `pointer_range_32` for atomics: if a load index has a statically negative constant (`sympy.expand(index).as_coeff_Add()[0] < 0`), the kernel uses 64-bit pointer arithmetic instead. Unskip `GPUTests.test_as_strided_past_input_extent`.

Do not globally disable buffer ops; only kernels that emit a negative offset take the slow path.

### Validation

Reproduced and verified on real AMD ROCm hardware:

- Hardware: Radeon RX 9070, gfx1201 · ROCm 10.0.0
- Eager: `[1., 2., …, 12.]`
- Compiled with #184232 rebase only: `[1., 1., 1., 1., 1., 1., 7., …, 12.]` (issue pattern)
- Compiled with this skip: matches eager
- Test: `test_as_strided_past_input_extent` (unskipped)

Claim limit: one consumer gfx1201 board, not the gfx950 CI runner.

---
*This is an experimental, AI-generated code change, reviewed by AMD engineers before submission.*
